principle: NN/g #1 Visibility of system status; NN/g #3 User control and freedom; WCAG 2.2 §2.4.11 Focus/Element Not Obscured (analogous)
location: /projects → PLANNER → COVERAGE heat-sink grid → gap-fill dialog ([role=dialog])
problem: REGRESSION of UX-1203. The gap-fill dialog is NOT a true viewport-bottom sheet on mobile. It has CSS `bottom: 60px` (correct, the v12 intent) BUT also carries an inline `top: -359.6px` from the desktop cell-anchoring logic, which wins. For any cell in the upper ~60% of the viewport the dialog renders with its TOP CLIPPED ABOVE y=0: measured top y=-87 (375) and y=-62 (414), with the × CLOSE button at y=-78 / y=-53 — OFF-SCREEN and UNREACHABLE. The dialog header/title is also clipped off the top. Only cells near the very bottom of the viewport (e.g. cell at y=532) render the dialog fully on-screen (y=158, close reachable). A mobile user who taps a typical gap cell sees almost nothing and cannot close the dialog except via Escape (which phones lack).
fix: On mobile (pointer:coarse or <768px) render the gap-fill dialog as a TRUE viewport-bottom sheet decoupled from the cell anchor: set `top: auto !important` (do not apply the cell-anchored inline top on mobile), `bottom: calc(60px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom))`, `left/right: 8px`, `max-height: 70vh`, with the dialog BODY (not the whole sheet) scrolling internally so the header + × close + WANT actions are always on-screen. The desktop anchored/flip-above popover should be branched off behind the same media query, not merged with the mobile sheet styles.

principle: WCAG 2.2 §2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum, 24px); Laws of UX — Fitts's Law; Refactoring UI — design for real content
location: /projects → PLANNER → COVERAGE heat-sink grid (default density on first load)
problem: PARTIAL REGRESSION of UX-1202. The grid DEFAULTS to FULL density on every fresh load (Condensed:aria-pressed=false, Full:aria-pressed=true), not Condensed as the v12 note claimed ("Condensed is the tapped default"). In Full mode every one of the 7,144 gap cells (each aria-label "…Tap to fill this gap.", i.e. genuinely tappable) renders at 12.6×12.6px on 375 (18 cols), 12.5px on 414 (21 cols), 12.4px on 768. That is ~half the 24px WCAG floor and far under 44px — and it is the FIRST thing a mobile user meets. Switching to Condensed DOES fix it (cells become tappable and the density is good) — so the Condensed path landed, but the wrong default is shipped and a brand-new recruit (0 owned paints) sees a wall of 12.6px cells.
fix: Default the coverage grid to Condensed (the tappable density) on coarse-pointer / <768px, and/or have Full mode enforce a cell `minmax(>=20px,1fr)` floor on mobile (reducing column count) so even the dense overview never drops below the 24px target. Full can stay the desktop default. Persist the user's density choice.

principle: WCAG 2.2 §2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum, 24px); Apple HIG 44pt; Material 48dp; Fitts's Law
location: /library → mobile card layout → per-row OWNED (○) and FAVOURITE (★) toggle buttons
problem: PARTIAL REGRESSION of UX-1204. The library mobile card rebuild (UX-1215) is good, but the owned/favourite toggles pinned to the right of each card measure 7.6×40px (Mark as owned) and 10.8×40px (Mark as wanted/favourite) — `padding: 0`, so the hit area is just the glyph width. Height ~40px is fine; WIDTH 7.6–10.8px is ~3× under the 24px WCAG minimum and ~5× under 44px. These are the highest-frequency repeated taps in the whole app (marking owned across a 7,144-paint catalog), so the mis-tap cost is severe. The v12 note claimed these now "fill the full grid cell (w-full h-full)" — that did not hold in the card layout.
fix: Give each toggle button horizontal padding (or a fixed `width: 44px`) so the hit area is ≥44×44px (min 24px). Keep the ○/★ glyph its current visual size, centered in the expanded target. The two toggles should be a 2-column 44px-each cluster at the card's right edge.

principle: Refactoring UI — design for real content (no clipping); WCAG 2.2 §1.4.10 Reflow; NN/g #4 Consistency
location: /wishlist → populated PAINTS row (TITLE | PRICE | P | STATUS table)
problem: Once a wishlist item exists, the paint row renders as a multi-column table too wide for the phone. The STATUS pill ('WISHLIST ▾') overflows to right=405 — 30px past the 375 viewport — inside a container whose overflow-x is hidden (scrollWidth 405 > clientWidth 360), so the status control is CLIPPED off the right edge and cannot be reached. 'OPEN IN ▾' is also crowded to the edge. Library got the card rebuild (UX-1215) but the wishlist row did not, so the same squeezed-table disease persists here on the primary mobile experience.
fix: Below 768px, render each wishlist row as a stacked card (title on its own line; price, P-flag, and the STATUS / OPEN-IN controls on a second wrapped line) exactly as the library card rebuild did. Reserve the multi-column table for ≥768px.

principle: Refactoring UI — design for real content; WCAG 2.2 §1.4.10 Reflow; NN/g #4 Consistency
location: /recipes → recipes list table (NAME | BODY | PALETTE | SLOTS | row actions)
problem: The recipes index renders as a horizontally-scrolling table on mobile (visible horizontal scrollbar; content overflows to right=386). The per-row actions (Assign ▾, Share) sit off-screen to the right and require horizontal scrolling to reach. Same un-reflowed-table problem as the wishlist row (UX-1304) and the pre-fix library (UX-1215). The card treatment was applied to library only.
fix: Below 768px, render each recipe as a stacked card (name + body chip + palette swatches on stacked lines, with New/Assign/Share as full-width or wrapped buttons), matching the library card pattern. Keep the table for ≥768px.

principle: NN/g #1 Visibility of system status; WCAG 2.2 §4.1.2 Name/Role/Value; Material — tab/segmented-control selected state
location: GLOBAL tab component — ATTACH RECIPE modal (Pick existing / Create new), recipe editor (Slots / Notes), planner density toggle (Condensed / Full)
problem: Segmented tabs/toggles across the app give NO active-state indication, visually or programmatically. ATTACH RECIPE 'Pick existing' vs 'Create new': after switching, both stay color rgb(245,245,245), font-weight 400, no border-bottom, transparent bg, and have no role=tab / aria-selected. Recipe editor 'Slots' vs 'Notes': identical (no border, no aria-selected). Planner 'Condensed' vs 'Full': identical styling — the active state lives ONLY in aria-pressed, which is invisible. Result: 'PICK EXISTING CREATE NEW' / 'SLOTS NOTES' read as run-on prose and the user cannot tell which view/density is selected (fails NN/g status visibility and exposes no state to AT).
fix: Give the active tab/segment a visible selected style (underline/border-bottom 2px in the accent, or filled background + bolder weight) AND correct semantics: role=tab + aria-selected on the modal/editor tabs; the density toggle already has aria-pressed but needs the matching visual treatment. Fix once in the shared tab/segmented-control primitive.

principle: WCAG 2.2 §2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum); Apple HIG 44pt; consistency with auth inputs
location: GLOBAL in-app form inputs — quick-add project (37px), recipe-name (37px), recipe search (35px), wishlist URL/title (37px), /tools/match hex (31px), /tools/gradient hex (31px), recipe STEP type <select> (25px)
problem: The P15/P16 touch-target sweep floored .btn / .btn-sm / .btn-md (via @media pointer:coarse → min-height 44px), but text INPUTS and SELECTs were not included. The sign-in/sign-up inputs are correctly 44px, but every in-app input/select renders 25–37px tall and is NOT covered by the coarse-pointer rule. The recipe-editor step-type <select> at 25px is the worst — a primary control in the editor. This is an inconsistency (auth 44px vs in-app 31–37px) and a sub-target on touch.
fix: Extend the coarse-pointer floor to inputs/selects: `@media (pointer: coarse) { .input, select, textarea { min-height: 44px } }` (or apply the existing .input token's mobile height). Confirm the recipe step <select> and tool hex inputs reach 44px.

principle: WCAG 2.2 §2.5.8 Target Size; Refactoring UI — affordance; Jakob's Law (chips look like chips)
location: /wishlist STATUS + CATEGORY filter rows (Wishlist/Purchased/Hold/All; Any/Box/Bits/Paint/Tool/Terrain/Other) and per-row Purchased/Hold actions
problem: Carryover of UX-1210 (explicitly deferred in v12 as 'outside the planner scope fence'). The wishlist filter rows render as plain wrapping inline-text buttons: 17px tall, no border, transparent bg — they read as a prose blob, not tappable filters, and the tap target is ~17px (well under 24/44). Per-row 'Purchased' (59×17) and 'Hold' (26×17) actions are the same. The planner brand chips WERE fixed to 44px in v12, but the wishlist/tools filter rows still carry the defect on the live primary mobile surface.
fix: Render these filters/actions as the same 44px tap-target chip primitive the planner now uses (visible border/background, ≥44px touch height, gap between, wrap cleanly). Apply the shared chip component so wishlist/tools/library inline filters match the planner.

principle: Laws of UX — Doherty Threshold; React correctness (SSR/CSR parity)
location: GLOBAL desktop/tablet status bar — live 'TIME · HH:MM:SS' clock (renders at ≥768 chrome)
problem: React minified error #418 (server/client HTML hydration mismatch) still fires during the session. UX-1206 fixed the /tools/eyedropper instance (direct nav to eyedropper at 375 is now console-clean — confirmed PASS), but #418 persists elsewhere. The most likely live source is the status-bar clock 'TIME·13:25:23' which renders a live time string and is present in the ≥768 desktop chrome (explaining why the 375 eyedropper check was clean). A hydration mismatch forces a client re-render and can transiently drop handlers.
fix: Gate the live clock behind useEffect (render an empty/placeholder time on the server, set the real time client-side) or add suppressHydrationWarning to the time node, and render it client-only. Verify the all-session console is #418-free afterward.
note: Clock was already placeholder-gated (useEffect-set, --:--:-- SSR default); added suppressHydrationWarning to the TIME node as the belt-and-suspenders fix the finding requests. If #418 persists, the source is elsewhere — needs a live console check.

principle: Refactoring UI — visual hierarchy / de-emphasise destructive; Von Restorff Effect; NN/g #5 Error prevention
problem: UX-1208 landed — DELETE PROJECT is now a solid red danger button with a confirm modal (good). But it has over-corrected: the bright-red filled button (rgb(255,71,87)) sits at the very top-right and is the single most visually salient element on the page, drawing the eye ABOVE the project title and the primary task (ADD UNIT / track progress). Von Restorff says the one different element is remembered — making 'delete' the loudest thing on a detail page over-weights destruction vs the user's actual goal and invites the eye to the hazard.
fix: Keep the destructive red semantics but lower its prominence: use a red OUTLINE/ghost variant (red text + border, transparent fill) rather than a solid red fill, and/or move it out of the prime top-right slot into a quieter position (e.g. bottom of the page or behind a '⋯ more' menu). Reserve the solid-red fill for the confirm-modal's final 'Delete forever' button (which already exists).
note: Applied the red OUTLINE tone (kept the top-right slot — moving placement is a layout decision; outline alone resolves the over-salience). Solid red reserved for the modal's Delete forever.

principle: WCAG 2.2 §2.5.8 Target Size; overlapping hit areas
location: /recipes/[id] → STEPS panel → step row controls (drag handle ≡, type <select>, ▸ expand, paint swatch, × delete)
problem: In the recipe-editor step row, the trailing controls OVERLAP: the paint-swatch button spans x=267→311 and the × delete button spans x=286→330 — a 25px horizontal overlap, so taps in the 286–311 band hit an ambiguous/overlapping target. (The play ▸, swatch and × are each 44px tall individually, but they're packed too tightly horizontally and collide.) Combined with the 25px-tall step type <select> (UX-1307), the step row is the most cramped control cluster on mobile.
fix: Lay the step-row trailing controls out with explicit gaps so their hit boxes don't overlap (flex with gap ≥8px, or wrap the swatch + delete onto a second line on narrow widths). Ensure the × delete has its own non-overlapping 44px box.

principle: NN/g #2 Match between system and real world; Apple HIG — clarity; label/aria divergence
problem: The three colour-launch buttons show the truncated visible label 'Start…' (full text is clipped) while carrying aria-label='Pick a shadow colour' etc. A sighted user sees only 'Start…' with no indication it opens a colour picker — the visible label is ambiguous and diverges from the (correct) screen-reader label. Truncation to 'Start…' on a 71px button conveys nothing.
fix: Give the button enough width (or shorter copy) to show a meaningful visible label that matches the aria-label, e.g. 'Pick' with a swatch/eyedropper icon, or 'Pick colour'. Avoid the trailing-ellipsis truncation on a label this short.

principle: Laws of UX — Von Restorff Effect; pricing-table convention; Aesthetic-Usability Effect
location: /pricing → tier cards (Free / Pro Monthly / Pro Lifetime / Founder)
problem: All four pricing tiers use identical neutral card styling. There is no visually highlighted 'recommended' tier (the universal pricing-table convention — Von Restorff). 'Pro Lifetime' (or Founder, capped at 100) is the obvious upsell but is given no extra emphasis, so the eye has no anchor and every tier competes equally. Content, copy and the honest 'checkout ships when Stripe lands' note are otherwise excellent.
fix: Highlight one recommended tier (e.g. Pro Lifetime or Founder) with a distinct border/accent glow + a 'Best value' / 'Most popular' ribbon, and order it visually as the anchor. Keep the others de-emphasised so the recommendation reads instantly.
note: Highlighted Pro Lifetime (the existing highlight flag) with a green Best value ribbon + accent-glow border. Did not reorder the grid — Pro Lifetime already sits centre-right; a reorder is a heavier layout decision left for a human if wanted.

principle: Polish / resource hygiene; NN/g #8 minimalist (no broken requests)
problem: Every page load logs a 404 for https://miniaturemanager.vercel.app/favicon.ico. The PWA manifest/app icons exist (verified healthy in v12), but the legacy /favicon.ico fallback is missing, so browsers that request it get a 404 on every visit. Cosmetic but it's a visible console error and a missed tab/bookmark icon on clients that fall back to /favicon.ico.
fix: Add a /favicon.ico (or a <link rel='icon' href='/icon.svg'> / app/icon route in Next.js app dir) so the root favicon request resolves 200. Verify no 404 in console after.

principle: Refactoring UI — chip affordance; WCAG §2.5.8 (target width)
location: /projects → PLANNER → COVERAGE brand-filter chips (All / AK Interactive / Citadel / …) and /tools/match brand-filter rows
problem: Minor follow-on to the v12 chip fix. The planner brand chips now correctly hit 44px tall (UX-1210 PASS for target size), but they still render with no border / transparent background (verified: border 0px, bg transparent), so they read more like a wrapping text list than discrete tappable chips — the affordance half of UX-1210 is only partially delivered. The /tools/match brand list uses full-width 32px rows (under 44 on touch, and not coarse-gated since it's a custom button, not .btn).
fix: Add a subtle resting border or background tint to the planner brand chips so they read as chips (Jakob's Law), and raise the /tools/match brand-filter rows to a 44px touch height on coarse pointers. Low priority — these are usable, just under-styled.
status_note: Planner brand chips now have a resting border-strong + 8% fg-muted tint fill with a distinct solid-amber active state; the planner density toggle keeps its visible filled-active state. The /tools/match brand rows are a non-planner surface outside this agent's scope fence (parallel agent owns non-planner findings).
